6-DOF Robotic Manipulator Arm

Lead Mechanical Engineer · Aug 2025 – Present
R@M-ARMOnshape · Ansys · SolidWorks FEA

I lead a team of 20+ engineers designing and manufacturing the rover's 1150 mm, 6-DOF manipulator arm, drone and science hardware (15+ hours a week), and I defend our design decisions at semesterly reviews in front of students and UMD engineering faculty. After a successful demo in the team's debut competition, we placed top 20 of 27 and finished ahead of every other first-year team.

Objective

Competition arm and rover

Earlier prototypes: early-stage concept and a potential metal version of the arm

  • Directed the subteam through the full design lifecycle, modeling assemblies in Onshape and producing detailed engineering drawings.
  • Integrated high-torque motors, position sensors, controllers and the camera into the mechanical structure, and owned the linkage design and fabrication schedule.
  • Designed carbon-fiber-reinforced nylon arm linkages and an aluminum sheet-metal, servo-driven parallel gripper, applying DFM and GD&T on Onshape engineering drawings.
  • Validated arm components with Ansys Mechanical and SolidWorks static structural FEA, then removed excess material and simplified joints, eliminating parts and fasteners and cutting material and part costs by 15%.
  • Fabricated with 3D printing, waterjet cutting, band sawing, drilling and tapping, with root-cause analysis on each prototype.
  • Next: running Ansys FEA on the manufacturing gripper.

Bioinspired Robotics Laboratory · UMD FIRE

Bio-inspired Underwater Vehicle

Undergraduate Student Researcher · Jan 2026 – Present
BRL-AUVSolidWorks · Tank testing

An autonomous underwater vehicle for structural inspection in the Chesapeake Bay. The design puts hydrodynamic efficiency and a reliable seal first. I own all of the SolidWorks CAD and 3D-print the hull, with a flexible TPU tail for propulsion.

  • Took the vehicle from concept to a working prototype in 2 weeks over 2 iterations, guided by 10+ peer-reviewed studies on dolphin fin kinematics.
  • Engineered a split hull with internal mounts that package sensors, motors and electronics, simplifying assembly and access for testing.
  • Developed the hull and tail propulsion design: prototyped a mold-injected fin, then moved to a flexible TPU tail.
  • Packaged sensors and motor drives into compact pressure housings, with CAD layouts that balance buoyancy and keep electronics dry.
  • Ran tank tests for sealing, endurance and buoyancy, then traced each leak to its root cause and redesigned until the hull was fully watertight.

Optical Parametric Oscillator Automation

ASPIRE Intern · Aug 2024 – Jun 2025
95%+cut in tuning time

Objective
Support infrared optical experiments and optimize wavelength conversion in a professional laser lab doing defense-adjacent research.

  • Built a Python automation tool that generated and analyzed 10,000+ data points to predict OPO configurations, taking tuning from several hours to under a minute (95%+ reduction).
  • Integrated the software with an optical spectrum analyzer to automate real-time data collection of signal peaks.
  • Used MATLAB to find failure modes and performance trends, and presented them to the engineers designing the infrared laser hardware.
  • Worked directly with a Ph.D. optical engineer on experiments and ran literature reviews in technical databases to support the method.
